gate_criteria.criterion: invalid manifests fail before any model request
gate_criteria.evidence: tests/contract/test_g01_gate.py::test_invalid_manifest_is_rejected parametrizes 11 distinct invalid manifests and requires a ValidationError from each; the CLI exits 1 on an invalid manifest and never reaches a transport. Unknown schema versions, unknown enum members, non-finite limits, duplicate IDs, retrying a 2xx, missing cost caps and smuggled credential fields are all rejected.

gate_criteria.criterion: a request cannot contain gold-answer or evaluator-only fields
gate_criteria.evidence: ModelRequest and PromptRef are both extra='forbid' at every nesting level; EVALUATOR_ONLY_FIELDS is asserted disjoint from the request schema; EvaluationPayload.assert_absent_from re-checks the serialized request; TaskSpec.safe_request re-verifies both the prompt hash and the absence of gold. Verified against pydantic escape hatches: a model_construct-built task still cannot dispatch a gold answer.

gate_criteria.criterion: every sample can be traced to its exact manifest and prompt
gate_criteria.evidence: trace_key binds manifest_hash and prompt_hash; GenerationResult carries manifest_hash (nullable, never backfilled) and a SampleKey; tests assert that changing stop sequences, the evaluator revision, the dataset revision, an item selection or any capability changes the relevant digest.

guards_added_for_defects: tests/unit/test_cli_shell.py::test_cli_shell_imports_no_third_party_dependency (keeps the CLI shell installable with no dependencies)
noted_not_a_defect: Set-valued fields (api_modes, context_lengths, stratify_by) are not order-canonicalized, so two semantically identical profiles can hash differently. Over-sensitivity is safer than under-sensitivity and the plan only requires key-order invariance, which holds. Left as-is deliberately.
resolved: PromptRef dropped `stop`, so two different dispatchable requests hashed to one identity, and TaskSpec.prompt_artifact_hash was never checked. Fixed: PromptRef.from_request round-trips every field, TaskSpec re-verifies the recorded hash at validation and again in safe_request(), and total_planned_requests/trace_key tests cover it.

title/description/comparability_rule accepted pasted credentials, and a test asserted the canary SURVIVED. Fixed: free-text fields are rejected on any secret marker, and the test now expects rejection.

credential_ref used a blocklist, so a JWT or bare hex key passed as a 'name'. Fixed: replaced with an allowlist of environment-variable names (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$), blocklist retained only for the error message.
GateEvidence certified a pass with zero passing tests or with a non-zero recorded command. Fixed: both are now rejected; a pass with real passes plus a skip is still allowed and disclosed.

FrozenModel claimed to be hashable and immutable but scoring_protocol was a mutable dict, so a validated manifest could drift under an already-recorded hash. Fixed: scoring_protocol is an immutable tuple of pairs that still serializes to a mapping, and the FrozenModel docstring now states exactly what frozen does and does not do.

planned_item_count returned 0 for an enumeration-only benchmark, silently disabling the request-cap check and surfacing a wrong planned_requests in the CLI. Fixed: it returns None, total_planned_requests returns None when any size is unknown, known_planned_requests gives the lower bound, an unmaterialized unknown size becomes an explicit dispatch blocker, and the CLI reports both.

source_revision.note: Includes the G00 revision plus the G01 schema layer; G00 remains valid because its own criteria were re-run unchanged on this tree.
source_revision.recompute_command: find . -type f \( -name '*.py' -o -name '*.toml' -o -name '*.md' -o -name '*.json' -o -name '*.yml' -o -name 'py.typed' -o -name 'constraints-dev.txt' \) -not -path './.venv/*' -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' -not -path './implementation/evidence/*' -not -path './implementation/tasks.json' | sort | while read -r f; do printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)" "${f#./}"; done | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1

T01A.evidence: test_campaign_schema.py covers incompatible versions, duplicate endpoint/benchmark/item IDs, non-finite prices and limits, conflicting limits, and credentials in credential_ref and in free text.

T01B.evidence: test_result_schema.py covers nullable usage (absent vs reported zero), retry/attempt collapse via accepted_sample_keys, unresolved attempts, and evaluator-only exclusion from requests.

T01C.evidence: test_manifest_hash.py covers key-order invariance at two depths, sequence-order sensitivity, and hash invalidation for seed, generation settings, limits, retry policy, campaign id, score version, materialization, item selection, evaluator revision, dataset revision, capabilities and prices.
